response_text: Exactly. Nothing is wrong with the runner. The Engineering Workspace is simply not cloned at ~/workspace/PASI-Engineering-Workspace on this machine. The command: Bash cd ~/workspace/PASI-Engineering-Workspace failed, and because Bash does not automatically stop after a failed cd, it continued executing git checkout, git pull, and python from: ~/workspace/personal-ai-system That is why your git pull fetched: https://github.com/th3-st0v3/personal-ai-system Set up the correct checkout Run: Bash cd ~/workspace git clone https://github.com/th3-st0v3/PASI-Engineering-Workspace.git cd ~/workspace/PASI-Engineering-Workspace git checkout main git pull --ff-only origin main pwd git remote -v ls scripts/pasi_168h_acceptance.py The last three commands should show, respectively, the Engineering Workspace path, the th3-st0v3/PASI-Engineering-Workspace remote, and the runner file. One important point PR #136 is still not merged. I verified that directly against GitHub. So don't launch the real 168h run yet. After #136 is merged, from the new checkout: Bash git pull --ff-only origin main python scripts/pasi_168h_acceptance.py --hours 168 --smoke Then the real launch: Bash PASI_PUSH=1 python scripts/pasi_168h_acceptance.py --hours 168 Your existing personal-ai-system checkout can remain where it is. Do not move or reuse it as the Engineering Workspace checkout. Once you have the new checkout, the next thing to verify is the smoke output before starting the seven-day run.
